title: Fuzzy-processing quantum computation
abstract: Quantum computation has attracted numerous attentions and develops rapidly in the recent decades. To against the decoherence and the control errors upon the qubits, quantum error corrections are adopted. Such approaches require lots of redundant qubits, accurate measurement and timely feedback. Here we investigate a new framework of quantum computation that is associated with fuzzy processing. It will benefit significantly from three aspects: the fuzzy recognition of qubit states reduce the required gate fidelity; the fuzzy encoding encodes the information of the qubits into a distribution of probability, suppressing the fluctuations in the output of long quantum circuits; the fuzzy feedback offers a more efficient way to control the qubits when precision information of quantum states are absent. Furthermore, the fuzzy processing can be integrated into quantum error correction, eliminating the need for immediate correction operations. The proposed scheme will be fairly suitable for the solution of decision problems, which has significant applications in the optimization problems and control problems.
summary: This paper introduces fuzzy processing as a novel paradigm for enhancing quantum computation robustness against decoherence and control errors. By encoding states into probability distributions and using fuzzy logic for state recognition and feedback, it significantly improves performance over traditional methods. This makes the framework highly promising for fault-tolerant quantum computing applications.
main_problem: The paper addresses decoherence and control errors in quantum computation by proposing a novel framework that integrates fuzzy processing into existing protocols.
main_result: Integrating fuzzy recognition, encoding, and feedback significantly improves the robustness of quantum circuits, allowing for high fidelity even when gate fidelities are imperfect or precise state information is unavailable.
method: The core method involves replacing exact quantum state representations with fuzzy probability distributions (fuzzy encoding) and using fuzzy logic rules to interpret noisy measurement outcomes (fuzzy recognition/feedback).
model_or_system: The model utilizes standard qubit systems undergoing unitary operations, specifically applied within the context of Quantum Error Correction (QEC) circuits involving multiple qubits.
key_observables: Average fidelity ($ ar{F}$), target qubit population ($P_L$), and output state distribution spread.
important_parameters: Noise intensity ($\lambda$ or $ eta$), number of gates ($N_g$), and the degree of gate infidelity ($1- ar{F}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that fuzzy set theory provides a mathematically sound framework to handle uncertainty, though it notes limitations regarding the inclusion of full decoherence effects.
figures_summary: Figures compare performance metrics (like $P_3(0)$ or $P_L$) for single-state versus fuzzy-encoded inputs under increasing noise/infidelity, consistently showing superior robustness for the fuzzy approach.
paper_structure: The paper builds conceptually by first introducing fuzzy recognition to reduce fidelity requirements, then detailing fuzzy encoding to stabilize output distributions, and finally integrating both into a full QEC framework using fuzzy feedback for robust control.
why_interesting: For AMO physicists studying open quantum systems, this work provides a mathematical toolset (fuzzy logic) to model and mitigate the effects of unavoidable measurement uncertainty and environmental noise in complex quantum hardware implementations.
